items.problem: Bootstrap overwrote the WinUI scaffold manifest, while validation omitted the required scaffold entry point and startup diagnostics discarded the managed frame.
items.evidence: session-log.txt lines 407-412 map Package.appxmanifest as migrate-as-is; lines 4123-4127 show missing UWP assets; lines 4190-4197 show repeated Arg_COMException; final active manifest used EntryPoint="LinguisticServices.App".
items.wrong_text_if_any: Initialize-UwpMigration.ps1 step 1 copied .appxmanifest directly to target even though MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md says to keep scaffold manifest values.
items.root_cause: Tier-1 bootstrap behavior contradicted the prose, and Tier-1 gates did not enforce or diagnose the remaining activation invariant.
items.proposed_fix: Preserve the UWP manifest under .uwp-source, keep the scaffold manifest active, validate EntryPoint="$targetentrypoint$", and retain/message-classify event 1026 stack evidence.
items.generalizes: Every packaged UWP-to-WinUI migration has an activation manifest, and copied UWP entry points/assets routinely build before failing registration or activation.

items.problem: Bootstrap ignored external files represented by MSBuild Include/Link metadata.
items.evidence: session-log.txt lines 329-346 report six copied files; source csproj lines 91-181 defines linked App/MainPage/styles/scenario XAML and assets; the agent spent turns 4-16 finding and recreating them.
items.skill_search: Link, linked files, external Include, SharedContent
items.root_cause: The initializer recursively copied only the source directory instead of reading the project item graph.
items.proposed_fix: Resolve external Compile/Page/ApplicationDefinition/Content Includes and copy them to explicit Link targets before rewrite/mapping.
items.generalizes: UWP solutions commonly share XAML, code, and assets through linked project items outside the entry-project directory.

items.problem: The skill instructed agents to run a nonexistent standalone `winapp build` command.
items.evidence: session-log.txt lines 3094-3150: command was not matched; CLI help exposed run but no build.
items.root_cause: The prose conflated benchmark build tooling with the standalone winapp CLI.
items.proposed_fix: Use `dotnet build <explicit-csproj>` throughout SKILL.md; reserve winapp/Test-AppLaunch for launch.
items.generalizes: Every migration must compile, and invalid command guidance wastes the first build cycle in any environment with the current CLI.
